Consult Summary:
34-year-old man with 3-day history of acute diarrhea (4–5 watery/loose stools daily), mild abdominal pain, one episode of vomiting, and possible low-grade fever. He remains orally hydrated; no red-flag features identified. Advised conservative management, oral rehydration, soft diet, and safety-netting instructions.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute self-limiting diarrhea – 3-day duration
- Frequency: 4–5 bowel motions/day; variable consistency (watery to loose)
- Associated symptoms: mild abdominal pain, single episode of vomiting, slight appetite loss, possible low-grade fever
- Pertinent negatives: no blood, no mucus, no recent travel, no suspicious food intake, able to maintain oral fluids
- Management discussed: soft/“BRAT-type” diet, avoid dairy (except yogurt), meat, eggs, fish until 48 h symptom-free; over-the-counter Dioralyte for oral rehydration
- Safety-net: seek review if >6–8 stools/day, blood in stool, symptoms >1 week, or signs of dehydration; stool sample and possible antibiotics if blood/persistent; hospital assessment if severe dehydration

Issue 2: Asthma (history)
- Currently uses “Lexapro” yellow inhaler (exact agent, dose, frequency not documented)
- No acute asthma symptoms reported today

Issue 3: Family history of colorectal cancer
- Father died of bowel cancer at age 62
- Not addressed in today’s plan; consider future colorectal cancer screening discussions

Medications:
- “Lexapro” inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies

Past Medical History:
- Asthma

Social History:
- Not discussed / not documented (smoking, alcohol, occupation, living situation unknown)

Preventative History:
- No preventive screenings or vaccinations documented

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or physical examination performed/documented (telehealth consult)

Plan:
- Implement soft diet; avoid meat, eggs, fish, dairy (except yogurt) until 48 h diarrhea-free
- Encourage adequate oral hydration; start Dioralyte oral rehydration salts (OTC) as needed
- Monitor stool frequency; if >6–8/day, blood present, or symptoms persist >1 week, arrange follow-up for stool culture +/- antibiotics
- Seek urgent care if signs of dehydration develop
- Consider future discussion on colorectal cancer screening given family history
- Review asthma medication details at next visit
